x: Match with Walton A.C. and Epsom H. at Walton on March 4th:—1, Nankeville (W), 30.7; 5, Davies (B), 30.35; 9, Bishop, 31.20; 11, Gray, 31.44; 17, Taylor, 32.46; 29, Cook, 36.36.

Bedford second and Derek Burfitt gave Nankeville a good run in the half mile. In the two miles team race we had the first three home, with Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Len Marchant finishing in line.

The 880 yards saw Archie Bedford and Jim Kennedy running for us but up against a strong Walton trio, which included Willie Nankeville, the A.A.A. mile champion, we had to be content with 4th place through Bedford, whereas Walton scored a “ maximum ” of 8 points for this race.

…n Bromley, Bill Lucas and Charles Walker finished a good second to the Poly and beat such clubs as Walton A.C., who had Nankeville running their final " leg," Cambridge H., South London H., Herne Hill H., Southgate H., Thames Valley H., and Woodford Green A.C.…
His time of 17 min. 23 secs. was only three seconds behind Pat Parker's fine run in 1938, and was the fastest of the day beating Nankeville's time by 3 seconds.

Jack Brown went next for us and he ran a well-judged race to catch the Walton man down the home straight, but Len Herbert could not hold Nankeville over the final leg, and we finished second in 17 min. 25 secs., which was only just outside the British (National) record of 17 min. 22.6 secs.

It was interesting to note that Nankeville only did 18.43. Our total time of 3.53.44 would have won the race on previous occasions, so it was not a question of our chaps failing, but of the other clubs improving.

"Jock" Cameron was 2nd in 51.2 secs., and Jack Brown won the 880, with Frank Wright in 2nd place in 1 min. 59.4 secs. Peter Bagnall was 2nd to Nankeville in a 4 mins. 15 secs 1 mile. and Chas. Walker won the 3 miles in 14 mins. 46.4 secs.
Wes Santee, America's hot favourite for that honour, was entered together with Chataway and Nankeville plus Lawrenz (Germany) and Ericsson (Sweden).
